group|REQ_ASYNC_PROVIDER_EXECUTION|Imple.name: Implementation
group|REQ_ASYNC_PROVIDER_EXECUTION|Imple.what: Async dispatch/await control flow must preserve the result. A dropped await or result write loses the result.

group|REQ_CREDENTIAL_RESOLUTION|Implemen.name: Implementation
group|REQ_CREDENTIAL_RESOLUTION|Implemen.what: Required/optional, fixed/auto, custom-name, and rotation branches can fail independently and must remain discriminated. A dropped rotation update or missing-key rejection breaks resolution without failing loudly. Key rotation computes the next key's position arithmetically (`offset % len(keys)`, `position + 1`); a swapped operator picks the wrong key. No threshold decides a credential: keys and names are matched, and rotation computes positions (`impl.arithmetic`), so `impl.boundary` does not apply.

group|REQ_CREDENTIAL_RESOLUTION|Specific.name: Specification / model
group|REQ_CREDENTIAL_RESOLUTION|Specific.what: Source partitions, deterministic rotation ordering, and public missing-key outcome are all normative semantics.

group|REQ_DOCUMENT_INPUT|Implementation.name: Implementation
group|REQ_DOCUMENT_INPUT|Implementation.what: Media-vs-text dispatch and result parsing are branch-sensitive; numeric thresholds are not the document contract. A dropped document-part write loses the document.

group|REQ_DOCUMENT_INPUT|Specification /.name: Specification / model
group|REQ_DOCUMENT_INPUT|Specification /.what: Wrong document facts or omission of a declared file-capable provider family violates the Requirement.

group|REQ_MULTIMODAL_CONTENT_NORMALIZATI.name: Implementation
group|REQ_MULTIMODAL_CONTENT_NORMALIZATI.what: Image bounds, branch selection, and ordered-part construction directly implement the normalized semantics. A dropped part append loses content or its order.

group|REQ_MULTIMODAL_CONTENT_NORMALIZATI.name: Specification / model
group|REQ_MULTIMODAL_CONTENT_NORMALIZATI.what: Wrong order/metadata, missing invalid-input partitions, or reject-after-provider ordering violates the Requirement.

group|REQ_MULTI_ROUND_TOOL_EXECUTION|Imp.name: Implementation
group|REQ_MULTI_ROUND_TOOL_EXECUTION|Imp.what: Multi-round execution is a state machine; skipping or terminating a branch can lose a required tool round or final response. A dropped tool-result append loses a round.

group|REQ_PROVIDER_ADAPTER_INTEROPERABIL.name: Specification / model
group|REQ_PROVIDER_ADAPTER_INTEROPERABIL.what: Omitting a supported provider family or returning a different normalized outcome violates the portability claim.

group|REQ_RATE_LIMIT_ROUTING|Interface /.name: Interface / protocol
group|REQ_RATE_LIMIT_ROUTING|Interface /.what: A blocked route must not be contacted and provider error status is a concrete public failure source.

group|REQ_REQUEST_OVERRIDE_PRECEDENCE|Im.name: Implementation
group|REQ_REQUEST_OVERRIDE_PRECEDENCE|Im.what: Layer precedence and explicit-null handling are implemented by branch/boundary decisions that must not silently invert. A dropped write of a merged value silently loses a layer. Precedence tells a given value from an omitted one and never compares a threshold, so `impl.boundary` does not apply; the omitted-versus-given tests are `impl.comparison`.

group|REQ_RESPONSE_NORMALIZATION|Specifi.name: Specification / model
group|REQ_RESPONSE_NORMALIZATION|Specifi.what: A wrong normalized result or a missing supported provider comparison violates portability.

group|REQ_ROUTE_ATTEMPT_LIMIT|Implementa.name: Implementation
group|REQ_ROUTE_ATTEMPT_LIMIT|Implementa.what: The contract is a numeric boundary implemented by truncation/comparison/control-flow decisions. A dropped attempt update or truncation removes the limit. The cap's only effect is the slice that cuts the candidate routes; losing it is the slice bound removed (`impl.boundary`), so `impl.effect` does not apply.

group|REQ_ROUTE_ATTEMPT_LIMIT|Specificat.name: Specification / model
group|REQ_ROUTE_ATTEMPT_LIMIT|Specificat.what: Minimum/intermediate limit partitions and the observable capped outcome are normative; route ordering itself belongs elsewhere.

group|REQ_ROUTE_TIMEOUT_FALLBACK|Impleme.name: Implementation
group|REQ_ROUTE_TIMEOUT_FALLBACK|Impleme.what: The configured timeout boundary and branch from timeout to fallback/terminal outcome are the implementation mechanisms under test. A dropped timeout raise or attempt record changes the outcome. The attempt's time limit is enforced by `Future.result(timeout=…)` and the router compares no time of its own, so `impl.boundary` does not apply.

group|REQ_ROUTE_TIMEOUT_FALLBACK|Specifi.name: Specification / model
group|REQ_ROUTE_TIMEOUT_FALLBACK|Specifi.what: Fallback-vs-terminal and sync-vs-async partitions plus timeout-before-next-attempt ordering are normative.

group|REQ_SENSITIVE_DATA_PROTECTION|Spec.name: Specification / model
group|REQ_SENSITIVE_DATA_PROTECTION|Spec.what: Wrong retained content, a missing artifact partition, or sanitization occurring only after persistence directly violates the product-level confidentiality outcome.

group|REQ_SESSION_LIFECYCLE|Implementati.name: Implementation
group|REQ_SESSION_LIFECYCLE|Implementati.what: Lifecycle branch/control flow selects whether and where history is copied or cleared; numeric comparison is not central. A dropped copy or clear leaves history shared or stale.

group|REQ_SESSION_LIFECYCLE|Specificatio.name: Specification / model
group|REQ_SESSION_LIFECYCLE|Specificatio.what: Wrong history, a missing lifecycle partition, or wrong before/after ordering directly violates the Requirement.

group|REQ_STRUCTURED_SCHEMA_CONTRACT|Imp.name: Implementation
group|REQ_STRUCTURED_SCHEMA_CONTRACT|Imp.what: Constraint comparisons/bounds and validation branches define accept/reject behavior. A dropped rejection raise accepts an invalid schema or value. Numeric schema constraints are enforced by the Draft 2020-12 validator (jsonschema), and the router compares no threshold of its own, so `impl.boundary` does not apply.

group|REQ_STRUCTURED_SCHEMA_CONTRACT|Int.name: Interface / protocol
group|REQ_STRUCTURED_SCHEMA_CONTRACT|Int.what: Caller schema/output shape is the data contract being validated.

group|REQ_STRUCTURED_TEXT_OUTPUT|Impleme.name: Implementation
group|REQ_STRUCTURED_TEXT_OUTPUT|Impleme.what: Schema-present/result-normalization control flow directly selects the structured path; numeric comparisons are not defining semantics. A dropped schema write sends an unstructured request.

group|REQ_STRUCTURED_TEXT_OUTPUT|Specifi.name: Specification / model
group|REQ_STRUCTURED_TEXT_OUTPUT|Specifi.what: A wrong structured result or an omitted supported provider family invalidates the claim.

group|REQ_SYNC_ROUTE_FALLBACK|Implementa.name: Implementation
group|REQ_SYNC_ROUTE_FALLBACK|Implementa.what: Fallback is a control-flow obligation; numeric thresholds are owned by the timeout/attempt-limit contracts. A dropped attempt record or terminal raise loses the fallback outcome.

group|REQ_TOOL_CHOICE|Implementation.name: Implementation
group|REQ_TOOL_CHOICE|Implementation.what: Named-choice control flow must not fall through to auto/alternate selection. A dropped tool-choice write falls back to automatic selection.

group|REQ_TOOL_RUNTIME_SAFETY|Implementa.name: Implementation
group|REQ_TOOL_RUNTIME_SAFETY|Implementa.what: The round-limit comparison/boundary and failure control flow are the implementation mechanisms that enforce bounded execution. A dropped round-limit raise or failure record removes the bound.

group|REQ_TOOL_RUNTIME_SAFETY|Specificat.name: Specification / model
group|REQ_TOOL_RUNTIME_SAFETY|Specificat.what: Failure vs limit partitions, termination ordering, preserved outstanding call, and public error outcome are normative semantics.

group|REQ_VIDEO_INPUT|Implementation.name: Implementation
group|REQ_VIDEO_INPUT|Implementation.what: Local-vs-remote media dispatch and provider translation are branch-sensitive. A dropped video-part write or upload call loses the video.

group|REQ_VIDEO_INPUT|Specification / mo.name: Specification / model
